I ran an exact-string search with the full text, ending at the closing quote, and it found one match in RoundCompanion_aug21b.html (line 6281, formData.append('prompt', ...)) and one in RoundCompanion_PLAYGROUND_p72_HAIKU.html (line 7085). The scripted parity check agrees (verbatim against both). The only thing that differs is the "source :4765" pointer in the code comment: the string sits at line 6281/7085 in these prototype files, not 4765. That is a comment and does not change the hint. Where the hint goes: - **Live path:** prepareSession always sends DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT in the realtime transcription session. - **Batch and recovery path:** transcribeAudio sends args.medicalHint || DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT. No client call passes medicalHint, so every caller gets the same hospital-oriented hint. The callers are: - Hospital rounding: AddPatient, quick dictation, PreRoundTab, encounter capture, encounter tasks. - Clinic: PreVisitTab, EncounterTab. - Nursing Home (SNF): PreRoundTab, encounter dictation. - The Ask modal. There are no per-surface vocabulary prompts. Whether the hospital vocabulary is right for Nursing Home is Q9 and is outside this verdict. Part (2) waits on the EVALUATION_FRAMEWORK.md copy, which is not under tools/qa-agent/uat/ at this commit.

code-review: partial → needs a person (partial: the half that can be checked passed, the other half needs another lane / a person / a file → a person looks)
At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server: (1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet; (2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls; (3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted". Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad. One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad. So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

No. At e02167f a Nursing Home resident has no facility field anywhere in the chain. The snf resident record (snfFields in convex/lib/validators.ts, which convex/schema.ts spreads into snfResidents) holds name, age, dob, sex, mrn, unit and so on, but no facility. snf:add takes exactly those fields as its args, so the mutation can't accept a facility either. The Add Resident form asks only for Full Name, Date of Birth, Unit / Room and MRN, plus Encounter Type. SnfPatientCard builds its identity line from unit, dob, age and mrn. matchesPatientSearch matches on name, room, unit, mrn and diagnosis. A case-insensitive search for 'facility' under apps/web finds only prompt text, billing labels and comments, never a data field. This is exactly the recorded gap known:no-facility. As the oracle says, U4's facility part and U6's facility field are a Fail on TFA-92581, not Blocked or not-built, and that holds whatever Q1 decides about where facility comes from. No open question is waiting on this, and the question's pass/fail rule agrees with the Then/Oracle.

Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

retry.ts sets CALL_BUDGET_MS=30_000, RETRY_DELAY_MS=1_000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=8_000 and RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS=10_000. Each attempt's deadline is attemptTimeout(elapsed) = max(8000, min(20000, 30000 − elapsed)). chat() passes that deadline into the Bedrock invoke, which enforces it with AbortSignal.timeout. The worst path: 1. Haiku attempt 1 gets a 20 s cap but fails with a temporary error at about 9.99 s. That is under 10 s, so the retry is allowed. 2. The 1 s pause brings the clock to about 11 s. 3. Haiku attempt 2 gets max(8, min(20, 19)) = 19 s and times out at about 30 s. 4. Mistral gets max(8, min(20, 30 − 30)) = 8 s (the floor), so the sequence ends at about 38 s. Other paths stay within about 30 s: - A first failure at 10 s or more skips the retry, and the fallback gets the rest of the budget: a 20 s timeout leaves Mistral 10 s, ending at 30 s. - A "model" failure skips the retry the same way. - After a fallback earlier in the same generate, Mistral is called alone with a 20 s cap. Because of the max() the fallback never gets less than 8 s, so that part of the Then is met. The computed worst case of about 38 s is above 30 s, and that is exactly the case the oracle hands to Q22. Skipping the Haiku retry after a slow temporary failure (10 s or more) is also handed to Q22 (AC 2). No recorded gaps apply. RT-07/RT-08 are static-lane context only, and as the oracle notes, RT-08 does not model the slow-first-failure path.

newspec-c: record-only → passed (record only (every judged cell passed; an open product issue is in the notes))
Re-run 16:49 JST after review (3/3 judged parts pass, as in 3 earlier runs). (a) passed on its then: device clock 23:58 -> M1, fast-forward past midnight -> M2; server has M1 once under 'Oct 14 (prior)', M2 alone in Most Recent, panel 'Oct 14 (prior) 1 lines' + 'Most Recent 1 lines'. (b)/(c) pass but are only PARTLY covered: the spec writes the recovery record and reopens the chart, so the failed line is neither in the open page's live transcript nor on the server and the app always takes the 'not held, append' branch; the re-append vs 'already archived' decision the oracle names (failed line still in the open page, most at risk after midnight) never runs and needs the cloud recording/transcription path. Not a plain pass because (a)'s then conflicts with U9 (UAT 3.8, not gated): only the device crossed midnight - the server day was still 2026-10-14 (UTC and Tokyo) - yet the stored transcriptDate is 'Thu Oct 15 2026' (the device's day) and M1 became a prior entry. S25's then expects that roll; U9 says the server clock decides. Quinn to rule which governs (cross-reference TC-16 S19, the wrong-clock phone step).
Product issue: If U9 governs: a physician whose device clock has passed midnight while the server's day has not (wrong clock, or a device ahead of the server day) records a bedside line; the line before it is moved to 'Oct 14 (prior)' and the new one is filed under the device's date (transcriptDate 'Thu Oct 15 2026' while the server day is 2026-10-14), for every device on the account. useEncounterCapture uses the device clock for the transcript day. Breaks UAT 3.8 / TC-16 U9 ('when a transcript becomes a prior entry ... use the server clock'); same root as the wrong-clock step of TC-16 S19 (a new finding against TFA-92594 per that oracle).

Product issue: When the summary comes back without background and studies: Hospital shows '✓ Note saved. Auto-updated: vitals, labs, hospital course' and restamps the background panel 'Updated 5:02 PM · Oct 14' directly under yesterday's one-liner 'Admitted with community-acquired pneumonia, improving on IV antibiotics.' (usePreRoundProcess.ts:394 sets admissionSummary.lastUpdatedAt = now even when no background came back), with yesterday's study 'Chest X-ray: right lower lobe infiltrate' still on the panel — so yesterday's text is labelled as updated today. Nursing Home shows only the 'Saved <time>' stamp, identical to a full success (its lastUpdatedAt is restamped too), so nothing tells the physician the panels were not refreshed. Breaks TC-10 U6 literal ('yesterday's panels are never silently reused'…

newspec-b: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Re-run 17:03. (a) both modes, thrown and 'unreadable': error shown, button back to 'Photograph', nothing saved, Paste works, Photograph retry works — but the error has no role=alert / live region (fails U15). The thrown read shows the raw server text (the mock mimics dev's Vertex 404; the app prints it verbatim). (b) Hospital passes: 'Prior note saved, but extraction failed. Expand it and tap Extract Fields to retry.' (role=alert), note kept; Extract Fields then fills imaging/background with no further tap. The primary-model fallback is proven in-process only (extractPriorNote Haiku ×2 → Mistral, diagnostics row Mistral fellBackFrom Haiku with providerMs); end to end it needs aiProvider:_set (out of bounds), so (b) is partly covered. Nursing Home stores the note with no extraction (Q4, recorded). (c) axe color-contrast (serious) on the panel heading in every state and view; date and note fields labelled only by placeholders; under the matrix's ≥ 24 px size rule the 'Note · <date>' toggle (276×16) and the delete button (21×21) are too small on Pixel 7 / iPhone 15 — but axe's target-size rule (WCAG 2.5.8, which allows the spacing exception) finds 0 violations in every state and view, so this is not a WCAG 2.5.8 failure. No sideways scroll, nothing truncated or covered.
Product issue: (1) A failed photo read is not announced to assistive technology (no role=alert / live region), and when the read service errors the physician reads '[CONVEX A(ai/vision:scanPriorNote)] [Request ID: …] Server Error Uncaught Error: Vertex AI request failed: 404 …' (TC-13 U15). (2) Previous Notes panel: low-contrast heading (axe color-contrast, WCAG 1.4.3) and placeholder-only labels on the date and note fields (WCAG 1.3.1/3.3.2) — TC-13 S28 oracle. Tap targets under the matrix's 24 px rule (16 px-high toggle, 21 px delete) on phones; axe target-size passes (spacing exception), so this is the matrix's rule, not WCAG 2.5.8. Observation: after a pasted note is saved, a photo read appends to the old text in the paste box (the note appears twice).

NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Legs error / empty / no-name / slow (35 s), both contexts: the right message shows ('The photo couldn't be read…' / 'No patients found in the image. Try a clearer photo.' / 'No residents found. Try a clearer photo.'), loading ends, nothing added. Slow leg, both contexts: loading visible at 3 / 15 / 30 s, message at ~35 s (Hospital re-run 18:00 JST, kept in evidence/history; NH from the 17:1x run). Retrying with the SAME photo starts no new read in every leg and context, on Chromium 151 (the file input still holds the file after a read, so no change event fires; the old message stays). With a byte-identical copy the retry adds its one row exactly once. NH double tap: Pecan 1, Rue 1, Quassia 0.
Product issue: After a failed or empty photo read, choosing the same image again ('Retake photo' in Hospital / 'Take Photo or Choose Image' in Nursing Home) starts no read and the old message stays, so the physician has to find or take a different photo. Shown on Chromium (desktop / Android WebView): the hidden file input is not cleared after a read (useCensusScan.ts handleImage / useResidentListScan never reset input.value), so the browser fires no change event for the same file. Breaks TC-02 S26 'lets the physician retry without retaking the photo' (oracle: a retry that needs the photo retaken is a Fail).
